prompt: Which formula expresses “Neither $P$ nor $Q$ is true”, equivalently $\neg(P\lor Q)$?

answers.explanation: Negating an inclusive “or” means each statement must be false. De Morgan’s law therefore changes or to and and negates both parts.
This asserts that at least one statement is true.
This asserts that both statements are true.
This requires only one part to be false, while “neither” requires both to be false.
An implication can be true with Q true; “neither” cannot.
This permits both statements to be true as well as both false.
This says “not both”, which still permits exactly one true statement.
This wrongly requires P to be true.
This wrongly requires Q to be true.
This requires different truth values, not two false values.
